error.signature: AI tells a non-EU visa holder they can submit their first permesso di soggiorno application by walking into the Questura, or treats the 8-day filing deadline as roughly a week of calendar days
error.regex: (permesso di soggiorno|italy residence permit deadline|8 (working )?days.*(italy|soggiorno)|kit postale.*soggiorno)

verdict.summary: Non-EU nationals staying in Italy more than three months must request a permesso di soggiorno within 8 working days of entry (giorni lavorativi, excluding Sundays and public holidays), per Article 5 of the Testo Unico Immigrazione (D.Lgs. 286/1998) and confirmed by Ministero dell'Interno guidance. For the main permit reasons, the application is not filed at the Questura counter directly: it is compiled using the yellow postal kit (kit a banda gialla) and submitted at a Poste Italiane branch offering Sportello Amico service, after which the applicant receives a Questura appointment for fingerprinting and biometric processing.

dead_ends.action: Advise a newcomer that they can submit their first permesso di soggiorno application by walking into the Questura in person
dead_ends.why_fails: Poste Italiane's official guidance routes first-issuance, renewal, conversion, and update requests for the listed permit reasons through the yellow postal kit submitted at a Poste Italiane branch with Sportello Amico service; the Questura visit that follows is a scheduled appointment for fingerprinting and biometric data collection, not the point of initial filing.
dead_ends.condition: First-time or renewal application for one of the permit reasons handled via postal kit
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the Questura front desk is the correct walk-in point for a first application, when it is actually only for the later fingerprinting appointment.

dead_ends.action: Treat the 8-day filing deadline as roughly a week of calendar days, or assume weekends and holidays count toward it the same as any other day
dead_ends.why_fails: Ministero dell'Interno's guidance and Article 5 of the Testo Unico Immigrazione (D.Lgs. 286/1998) both specify the deadline as 8 giorni lavorativi (8 working days), explicitly excluding Sundays and public holidays - so the actual calendar window is longer than a literal 8-calendar-day count would suggest, and miscounting it either way risks filing late or being told (incorrectly) that the deadline has already passed.
dead_ends.condition: Calculating the filing deadline after entry into Italy
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the 8-day rule is measured in calendar days rather than working days, or that it is an informally-enforced guideline.

workarounds.action: Get the yellow kit (kit a banda gialla) from any Poste Italiane branch as soon as possible after entry, complete it, and submit it at a branch offering Sportello Amico service within 8 working days of entry
workarounds.how: Total costs typically include a EUR 16 revenue stamp, roughly EUR 30 for the post-office operator, about EUR 30.46 for permit production, plus permit-type-specific contributions. Submission produces a receipt allowing continued lawful presence in Italy while the application is processed, plus a Questura summons letter with a date, time, and location for the fingerprinting appointment.
workarounds.condition: Within 8 working days of entry into Italy

workarounds.action: If unsure whether a specific circumstance uses the postal-kit route or requires filing directly with the competent Questura, check the Ministero dell'Interno's guidance for that permit reason before the 8-working-day window closes

frequently_confused_with.distinction: This canon covers the deadline and postal-kit procedure for filing the permesso di soggiorno itself; the other covers which office assigns the codice fiscale and when it comes bundled with that same permit application.
